A_target.statement:
Let $a, n \in \Z$ with $n > 0$ and $a \perp n$.
Then:
:$a^{\map \phi n} \equiv 1 \pmod n$

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] of [[Definition:Order of Structure|order]] $m$.
Then:
:$\forall g \in G: g^m = e$

validity_conditions: The residues coprime to n form a group (Z/nZ)^* under multiplication, of order phi(n).
Every element g of a finite group satisfies g^{|G|} = e (order divides group order).
Instantiate with G = (Z/nZ)^*, g = a to get a^{phi(n)} = 1 mod n.
proof_plan: The [[Definition:Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues|group of reduced residues]] $\paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times$ is a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] of order $\map \phi n$.

By [[Element to Power of Group Order is Identity]], which follows from [[Lagrange's Theorem (Group Theory)|Lagrange's Theorem]]:
:$\forall g \in \paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times: g^{\map \phi n} = \eqclass 1 n$
